f1-initial.aria: Figure 1. The 20 participants of the pilot trial and the ideal bootstrap distribution of the difference in means. Its standard deviation, the bootstrap standard error, is 3.16 mmHg, and its middle 95% runs from 1.3 to 13.7 mmHg.

f2-initial.aria: Figure 2. The ideal bootstrap distribution of the difference in means for the pilot data, with the t distribution the t interval reads its limits from drawn on the same scale. Percentile interval 1.3 to 13.7, BCa 1.3 to 13.7, t interval 0.5 to 14.5 mmHg.

f3-initial.aria: Figure 3. Normal outcomes, 10 per arm: the first 100 of 1,000 simulated percentile intervals, 4 of which miss the true difference, and the coverage of each method over all 1,000 trials: t interval 94.4%, percentile 90.6%, BCa 90.4%, bootstrap-t 95.1%.
